integrity.classification_basis: After q=d-1, parity of n reduces the comparison to two explicit positive expressions; quadrics are handled separately.
integrity.dual_degree_basis: The inspected Chern-Mather duality paper explicitly recovers classical degree-of-dual and dual-defect formulas; the smooth hypersurface specialization is d(d-1)^n.
integrity.euler_basis: The tangent-normal exact sequence and Gauss-Bonnet give the displayed Chern coefficient, which simplifies to the closed Euler formula.

scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes a smooth complex projective hypersurface.
The comparison uses absolute topological Euler characteristic, not a signed comparison in odd dimension.
Both invariant formulas are classical, so an older unindexed source may contain the same elementary comparison.
title: A unique dual-degree–Euler equality for smooth hypersurfaces
